column1: # What the shipping command validator accepts, one row per value offered to it.
# That validator is the retired connector's, and these rows were taken by running
# it rather than by reading its conditionals.
# Columns: command, argument, type, value, refused, reason. refused is true when
# the validator rejected the value for the value's own sake. reason is the error
# it gave, and is empty on an accepted value.
# A refusal about anything else, a required argument that is missing or a printer
# state that forbids the command, says nothing about the value, so such a value
# is recorded here as accepted. While one argument was offered a value, every
# other argument of the command carried a value the validator had already
# accepted, because a command missing a required argument is refused before any
# The values offered straddle every bound the validator enforces, one on each
# side, and add the shapes it refuses for what they are rather than for how large
# they are. Every model was probed at firmware 6.4.0 and the commands were
# unioned: no model has all of them, and the bounds are firmware struct sizes and
# protocol widths rather than per-model rules.
# internal/connector/xbuddy/limits_test.go compares the argument bounds in
# verbs.go with these rows, and fails on a difference that is not listed there
